desk_read: Yesterday's session showed a clear divergence across asset classes as energy markets attracted fresh capital while equities and precious metals saw liquidation. Natural Gas saw heavy participation with volume running at 1.5x its 20-day average alongside a price increase of +3.89% and new longs entering the market. In contrast, S&P 500 futures fell -0.33% with total open interest dropping by -8.0k contracts (-0.4%) amid long liquidation and volume at 0.8x its 20-day average. Silver also faced strong selling pressure with a price drop of -3.72% accompanied by new shorts as total open interest rose +5.4k contracts (+4.6%). Meanwhile, Brent (NYMEX) gained +3.30% with total open interest up +4.3k contracts (+3.4%), reflecting persistent backwardation and new longs.
oil_read: During yesterday's session, WTI (most active CLZ26) rose +2.55% with total open interest across all months up +900 contracts (+0.1%) and volume at 0.8x its 20-day average, signaling new longs in backwardation with the CLZ26-CLK27 spread at +7.12 $/bbl. Brent (NYMEX, most active BZF27) gained +3.30% alongside a total open interest increase of +4.3k contracts (+3.4%) and volume at 0.6x its 20-day average, also showing new longs in backwardation with the BZF27-BZM27 spread at +9.36 $/bbl.
bias_read: WTI Crude Oil shows a bullish bias with fresh longs and a steepening backwardation, while Brent shows a mildly bullish bias with new longs on light volume 0.6x the 20-day average. This positioning supports the current crude trend, though Brent's low participation warns of a lack of broad momentum. Natural Gas presents a mildly bullish bias with new longs and high volume 1.5x the 20-day average, signaling strong conviction that supports the move. Conversely, Gold displays a neutral bias from long liquidation, warning of potential exhaustion in recent upside. Across the broader desk, mixed participation suggests traders are selectively committing capital rather than driving a unified cross-asset trend.
